sentences.en: So tell us about what the psychopath effect is.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲什么是精神病态效应吧。

sentences.en: So we talk a lot about psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 我们经常讨论精神病态。

sentences.en: It's one of those issues within psychology that everybody has an opinion on and everybody feels like they understand it.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学中那些人人都想发表意见、人人都觉得自己懂一点的问题之一。

sentences.en: But it's like so many other things in science and in psychology specifically that we all understand it.
sentences.zh: 但它就像科学特别是心理学中的许多其他事情一样，我们都觉得自己懂了。

sentences.en: But often we're wrong.
sentences.zh: 但往往我们都错了。

sentences.en: So psychopathy as a psychological function, rather than thinking of it as a disorder, psychologists now classify it as a collection of behaviours.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一种心理功能，心理学家现在不再把它看作一种障碍，而是将其归类为一系列行为的集合。

sentences.en: So we have meanness, boldness and disinhibition.
sentences.zh: 具体包括：卑劣性、大胆性和去抑制性。

sentences.en: So meanness is your archetypal psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 卑劣性就是你典型的精神病态特征。

sentences.en: That's the thing you think of when you think of psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 这就是你一想到精神病态时脑子里浮现的东西。

sentences.en: So it's that antagonism, that low empathy, resource hoarding, tending to be cruel.
sentences.zh: 也就是对抗性、低同理心、资源囤积以及倾向于残忍。

sentences.en: Boldness, on the other hand, is something that we tend to like.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，大胆性则是我们往往比较喜欢的特质。

sentences.en: So it's the tendency to be
sentences.zh: 也就是

sentences.en: low fear, low stress.
sentences.zh: 低恐惧、低压力的倾向。

sentences.en: People tend to be confident, they tend to be charming.
sentences.zh: 这类人往往很自信，也往往很有魅力。

sentences.en: These are the kind of people who tend to function very well in society.
sentences.zh: 他们正是那种在社会中能如鱼得水的人。

sentences.en: And then disinhibition are the kind of people who tend to struggle more in society.
sentences.zh: 而再去抑制性则是指那些在社会中更容易苦苦挣扎的人。

sentences.en: They have trouble controlling their impulses.
sentences.zh: 他们难以控制自己的冲动。

sentences.en: They're more likely to have a criminal background, relationship issues, just because they don't have that inhibitory capacity that hopefully the rest of us do.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能有犯罪背景、人际关系问题，仅仅是因为他们缺乏我们其他人所具备的那种抑制能力。

sentences.en: We talk a lot about what the psychopath is.
sentences.zh: 我们总是谈论精神病态者是什么样的。

sentences.en: But what fascinated me more than that was, what effect do they have on the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 但比这更让我着迷的是：他们对我们其余人产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: As we go through the book, so the book is organised in terms of first glancing at a psychopath across a crowded room,
sentences.zh: 当我们翻阅这本书时会发现，这本书的结构是这样的：首先是在拥挤的房间里匆匆瞥见精神病态者一眼，

sentences.en: getting to know them, maybe getting into a friendship with them, becoming colleagues,
sentences.zh: 然后是了解他们，或许与他们建立友谊，成为同事，

sentences.en: romantic relationships, if the psychopath is a parent.
sentences.zh: 发展浪漫关系，以及如果精神病态者是父母的话会怎样。

sentences.en: So it follows our progress through the relationship with the psychopath.
sentences.zh: 所以它遵循了我们与精神病态者交往的发展历程。

sentences.en: And what was so interesting to me is that in each of those stages, they have different effects on us.
sentences.zh: 对我而言最有趣的是，在每一个阶段，他们对我们都会产生不同的影响。

sentences.en: So they have a pronounced capacity to affect our cognitions, our emotions, even our sense of reality, you know, what we understand the world and ourselves to be.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们有着显著的能力去影响我们的认知、情感，甚至是我们的现实感，你知道的，也就是我们对世界和自我的理解。

sentences.en: So the psychopath effect is about psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 所以，精神病态效应是关于精神病态本身的。

sentences.en: But more than that, it's about us.
sentences.zh: 但不仅于此，它更是关于我们自己的。

sentences.en: And it's about how we react to psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 它是关于我们如何对精神病态作出反应的。

sentences.en: Thank you, I really enjoyed the book.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，我真的很喜欢这本书。

sentences.en: And I really liked the way that it was structured with those kind of different relationships.
sentences.zh: 我也非常喜欢它围绕那些不同人际关系展开的结构方式。

sentences.en: And one of my favourite bits was that you used kind of real life examples of people who probably would have scored quite highly high profile people,
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的片段之一是，你使用了现实生活中的真实案例——那些可能得分相当高、备受瞩目的人物，

sentences.en: for example, there was someone that had been a big player in kind of the, the kind of Nazi movement was in it.
sentences.zh: 例如，书中提到了一个曾在纳粹运动中扮演重要角色的人。

sentences.en: And I just found that really helped me to think, right, okay, yeah, I can see how that plays out.
sentences.zh: 我发现这真的很有帮助，让我觉得：对，没错，我能看出这在现实中是如何上演的。

sentences.en: But also, it was really helpful to think, actually, these might be people that we'd meet
sentences.zh: 而且这也非常有启发性，让我意识到，实际上这些可能正是我们在职场晋升路上

sentences.en: on our way up in a career, or we might be, you know, shoulder to shoulder trying to go for the same jobs, and how that's going to impact us.
sentences.zh: 会遇到的人，或者我们可能会肩并肩去争取同一份工作，而这将会对我们产生影响。

sentences.en: So I really liked that kind of real world kind of how to spot a psychopath aspect as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很喜欢这种现实世界中“如何识别精神病态”的视角。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's part of how our understanding of psychopathy has changed, because we've traditionally,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这正是我们对精神病态的理解发生改变的一部分原因，因为过去传统上，

sentences.en: because psychopathy was treated as a disorder, these weren't the kind of people that we'd rub shoulders with, you know, in the book, I talk about the extremes.
sentences.zh: 由于精神病态被当作一种障碍来对待，这些人并不是那种我们会与之擦肩而过的人，你知道的，我在书里讨论过极端情况。

sentences.en: So like Ted Bundy, you know, the, the kind of people who you read about in the news.
sentences.zh: 比如泰德·邦迪，你知道的，也就是你在新闻里读到过的那种人。

sentences.en: But odds are, you're not going to bump into those, you know, you're statistically, you'd be quite unlucky to meet a Ted Bundy.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你不太可能会撞见他们，从统计学上讲，你要是能遇到一个泰德·邦迪，那可真够倒霉的。

sentences.en: But as our understanding of psychopathy has evolved, we've realised that the lower levels of psychopathic traits tend to affect all of us,
sentences.zh: 然而，随着我们对精神病态理解的演变，我们意识到较低水平的精神病态特质往往会影响到我们所有人，

sentences.en: you know, the, what we can call a dimensional personality traits.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们所说的维度人格特质。

sentences.en: So meanness, boldness and disinhibition, we all have those traits.
sentences.zh: 所以，卑劣性、大胆性和去抑制性，我们所有人身上都有这些特质。

sentences.en: You know, we are, we all have a certain level of meanness within us.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们每个人体内都有一定程度的卑劣性。

sentences.en: We all have a certain level of boldness and of disinhibition.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都有一定程度的大胆性和去抑制性。

sentences.en: The difference is, when we're talking about somebody who would score as a psychopath, is that they're looking at higher levels of those behavioural traits.
sentences.zh: 区别在于，当我们谈论那些会被评定为精神病态的人时，他们表现出的是更高水平的这些行为特征。

sentences.en: But it is very much a societal issue.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是一个社会性问题。

sentences.en: You know, and as, as we're, as you saw in the book, I interviewed people who's, who had real life experiences with people high in psychopathic traits.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你在书中所看到的，我采访了那些在现实生活中与高精神病态特质人群有过接触的人。

sentences.en: And there was no shortage.
sentences.zh: 这样的人并不少见。

sentences.en: And the fun thing is, you say, I'm writing a book about psychopaths, and everybody, everybody will say, well, there was this guy.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当你对别人说“我在写一本关于精神病态者的书”时，每个人、真的每个人都会说：“哦，我认识这么个人。”

sentences.en: You know, everybody has a story.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每个人都有一个故事。

sentences.en: It's so interesting what happens when you remove the disorder element.
sentences.zh: 当你剥离掉“障碍”这一元素时，所发生的事情真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: You know, when you start looking at the subclinical, just below that threshold, how much it kind of proliferates out and how, how pronounced of an issue it becomes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当你开始审视亚临床群体——也就是刚好在那个门槛之下的群体时，你会发现这种影响扩散得有多么广泛，它变成了一个多么显著的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think your book has changed the way I think about people, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，你的这本书确实改变了我对人的看法。

sentences.en: Is that, is that a good thing?
sentences.zh: 这是件好事吗？

sentences.en: Or have I ruined people for you?
sentences.zh: 还是说我对人的看法被你彻底毁掉了？

sentences.en: Well, a little bit of both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，两者皆有一点吧。

sentences.en: A little bit from column A, a little bit from column B.
sentences.zh: A栏有一点，B栏也有一点。

sentences.en: Even the conversation I was having in, in the hairdressers on Friday, you know, about antagonism.
sentences.zh: 甚至我在周五理发时进行的谈话，也是关于对抗性的，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like, I think the word antagonism is ruined for me now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得“对抗性”这个词现在对我已经彻底毁了。

sentences.en: It's never going to make me not, oh, right.
sentences.zh: 每当遇到事，我脑子里总会蹦出：哦，对。

sentences.en: Okay, let's have a little look at that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们仔细看看这个。

sentences.en: But it's, it's because I do a lot of work with people who've experienced complex trauma.
sentences.zh: 但这是因为我做了很多针对经历过复杂创伤的人群的工作。

sentences.en: So we've often met people that are really not good people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常会遇到那些确实算不上好人的人。

sentences.en: It's really helped me think about formulating with them in a different way.
sentences.zh: 这本书真的帮我以一种不同的方式去为他们进行心理建构（formulation）。

sentences.en: Like it was never your fault.
sentences.zh: 比如，这一切从来都不是你的错。

sentences.en: And maybe, you know, there was never maybe anything you could have done that was any different once you'd kind of been locked in their sights.
sentences.zh: 而且也许，一旦你被他们锁定在视线范围内，你无论怎么做可能都无法改变任何结果。

sentences.en: And I think that that can be very de-shaming in itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为这本身就能极大地消除受害者的羞耻感。

sentences.en: And kind of putting that responsibility firmly outside of, of your control and back, and back into the court of the person with the high psychopathy score.
sentences.zh: 并且把这种责任牢牢地从你的控制范围之外剥离出去，重新归咎到那个精神病态高分者的头上。

sentences.en: And what's so interesting, so when I started researching the book, the one thing I knew
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，当我开始研究这本书时，我唯一确切知道

sentences.en: I wanted to talk about was what happens if you have somebody with high psychopathic traits who is a parent.
sentences.zh: 我想探讨的事情就是：如果一个具有高度精神病态特质的人成为了父母，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And my comfort blanket for anything is the research.
sentences.zh: 对于任何事情，我的精神慰藉都是查阅研究资料。

sentences.en: So when I wanted to understand what that looked like, I went straight into the psychological research.
sentences.zh: 所以当我想要了解那是什么样的情况时，我直接深入到了心理学研究中。

sentences.en: And there was nothing.
sentences.zh: 结果却是一无所获。

sentences.en: There were a handful of studies.
sentences.zh: 只有寥寥可数的几项研究。

sentences.en: I spoke to one brilliant researcher, Adele Forth, who was in Carleton University in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我联系了一位杰出的研究员阿黛尔·福斯，她在加拿大卡尔顿大学工作。

sentences.en: And she was incredibly helpful and has done the study on parental psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 她给予了极大的帮助，并且做过关于父母精神病态的研究。

sentences.en: But it was stunning that it was a case of the study.
sentences.zh: 但令人震惊的是，这几乎成了“孤本研究”。

sentences.en: You know, there was so little research done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，相关的研究实在太少了。

sentences.en: And for those people, I started doing a series of interviews because I had to find out myself because there just wasn't anything there.
sentences.zh: 由于资料的匮乏，为了弄清真相，我只能开始进行一系列采访。

sentences.en: And what was so fascinating with these individuals who had been raised by somebody who they can now identify as having psychopathic traits, is they had gone through life
sentences.zh: 而这些由可以被他们明确识别出具有精神病态特质的人抚养长大的个体，其经历是如此令人着迷：他们度过了一生，

sentences.en: never knowing what was wrong, but always feeling that there was something wrong with them.
sentences.zh: 却永远不知道问题出在哪里，但总是觉得自己身上有什么毛病。

sentences.en: And what you would see is they had gone to, they would have histories of anxiety, depression, PTSD, chronic ill health.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，他们有着焦虑、抑郁、创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）以及慢性健康问题的病史。

sentences.en: And they would go for psychological support, always saying there's something wrong with me.
sentences.zh: 他们会去寻求心理支持，总是说“我身上出了问题”。

sentences.en: And what happened when they were unable, when they were able to correctly locate the problem, when they were able to say, actually, perhaps the problem wasn't me, perhaps
sentences.zh: 而当他们能够正确地找到问题所在，当他们能够说“其实，也许问题不在我，也许

sentences.en: the problem was that my parent had psychopathic traits, which massively influenced the way in which they parented me.
sentences.zh: 问题在于我的父母具有精神病态特质，这极大地影响了他们抚养我的方式”时，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: And what happened then was really quite fascinating.
sentences.zh: 随之发生的事情真的相当引人入胜。

sentences.en: In terms of mental health, they were able to function in a far more, far more healthy way, they were able to, there's something,
sentences.zh: 在心理健康方面，他们能够以一种远为健康的方式生活，他们能够……有一种感觉，

sentences.en: there's something really powerful about that saying it wasn't about me.
sentences.zh: 那种说“这与我无关”的话语中蕴含着真正强大的力量。

sentences.en: You know, it was about them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这与他们有关。

sentences.en: And what the research suggests is that even if they didn't remove themselves from their parent,
sentences.zh: 研究表明，即便他们没有从父母身边抽身离开，

sentences.en: you know, we're talking about adults now, but most of them maintained relationships with the
sentences.zh: （我们现在讨论的是成年人，但他们大多数人与那些

sentences.en: psychopathic parents, a lot of them, the majority of them looked after them in their old age.
sentences.zh: 有精神病态的父母保持着联系，其中很多人、大多数人在父母年迈时还照顾了他们），

sentences.en: But even doing that, even still being in that environment, the difference in mental health, when you can locate the problem, as opposed to when you think it's you, is staggering.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，即使依然身处那种环境中，当你能够指出问题所在，而不是认为问题出在自己身上时，心理健康状况的差异是令人震惊的。

sentences.en: There's something really powerful about being able to say this didn't start with me.
sentences.zh: 能够说出“这一切并非由我而起”，这种能力本身就具有真正强大的力量。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also almost that you can choose to not be riled or choose not to be affected or choose to
sentences.zh: 而且差不多你也可以选择不被激怒，选择不受影响，或者选择

sentences.en: mildly dissociate in order to get through to just be able to do the physical care jobs associated with looking after your parents.
sentences.zh: 轻微地解离，以便能够应付过去，仅仅去应付照顾父母所涉及的那些日常体力活。

sentences.en: But know that actually, this isn't about me.
sentences.zh: 但要知道实际上，这并不是针对我。

sentences.en: You know, any other child that been born or in their in their power would have likely had the same experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，任何其他出生的孩子或者只要在他们自己能力范围内的孩子，很可能会有同样的经历。

sentences.en: And it wasn't my fault and I deserve something different.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是我的错，我值得拥有更好的对待。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, in terms of it's so difficult, I think for those, that was the group that affected me more than any other, because their
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，就它有多困难而言，我认为对那些人来说，那是比其他任何群体都更深地影响了我的群体，因为他们的

sentences.en: entire, their identity, their worldview, everything had been built by a psychopath.
sentences.zh: 全部，他们的身份，他们的世界观，一切都是由一个精神病态者构建的。

sentences.en: That's a really dangerous place to be.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常危险的处境。

sentences.en: And, you know, we, we, we think of psychopaths as being bad guys, because that's what society has kind of taught us.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们，我们，我们认为精神病态者是坏人，因为那是社会教导我们的。

sentences.en: But all of these people, all of the psychopathic parents showed evidence of loving behaviours, generosity, kindness.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些人，所有的精神病态父母都表现出了充满爱意的行为、慷慨和善良。

sentences.en: So it wasn't a dichotomy.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是非黑即白的。

sentences.en: You know, there was this real contradiction in terms going on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里面存在着真正的矛盾。

sentences.en: And it was really confusing then for the children going, well, they can't be a psychopath because they gave me, you know, money to, they supported me
sentences.zh: 所以对孩子们来说真的很困惑，他们会想，嗯，他们不可能是精神病态者，因为他们给了我，你知道的，钱去，他们支持我

sentences.en: through university or they gave me money to buy a car.
sentences.zh: 读大学，或者他们给我钱买车。

sentences.en: But the, the problem I think we always have in those situations is that when we find ourselves presented as an adult with a psychopathic parent,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得我们在这些情况下总会遇到的问题是，当成年后的我们发现自己面对着一个有精神病态倾向的父母时，

sentences.en: we're often not approaching them as an adult.
sentences.zh: 我们往往并不是以成年人的心态在接近他们。

sentences.en: We're approaching them as a child again, because they bring up every, I mean, you know, and obviously this is your area, you know, they bring up all of these childlike heartbreaks.
sentences.zh: 我们是以孩子的姿态重新接近他们，因为他们勾起了所有——我的意思是，你知道，这显然是你的领域，你知道的——他们勾起了所有这些童年时期的心碎。

sentences.en: And so when they trigger us, I love the fact you used the word mild
sentences.zh: 所以当他们触发我们时，我很喜欢你用了“轻微”这个词，

sentences.en: dissociation, because I think it very much is that there is a part of us choosing to go, okay, think
sentences.zh: “解离”，因为我认为这非常贴切，有一部分我们在选择去想，好吧，想想

sentences.en: about sheep, or, you know, I'm Welsh, we think about sheep, you know, anything just to kind of,
sentences.zh: 绵羊，或者，你知道的，我是威尔士人，我们会想到绵羊，你知道的，任何事情，只要能够

sentences.en: to remove yourself from that bombardment of pain, to remove yourself from being a small child again in that environment and unable to escape.
sentences.zh: 让自己从那种痛苦的狂轰滥炸中抽离出来，让自己不再是那种环境中无法逃脱的小孩子。

sentences.en: You know, there's a, there's a lot, it's a very powerful message to be able to say, I'm having a boundary.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这有很多，能够说“我要划清界限”是一个非常强有力的信息。

sentences.en: I'm setting a boundary because it gives you that sense of control that you didn't have as that small child.
sentences.zh: 我正在划定界限，因为它能给你一种作为那个小孩子时所没有的掌控感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think speaking as a parent myself, like, I would consider my job, you know, well done or done enough, if my children ultimately
sentences.zh: 我想作为一个父母来说，我会认为我的工作，你知道的，完成得很好或者说足够好了，如果我的孩子们最终

sentences.en: choose to have me in their lives when they're grown, but that they don't need to have me in their lives, because they're not dependent, and that we're not enmeshed.
sentences.zh: 选择在他们长大后让我的生活里有他们的存在，但他们并不“需要”我的存在，因为他们并不依赖我，而且我们并没有纠缠在一起。

sentences.en: You know, I want them to, you know, choose to come out and have coffee or go to the cinema with me or come around for dinner,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我希望他们，你知道，选择出来跟我喝咖啡，或者去看电影，或者来家里吃晚饭，

sentences.en: or my youngest always says, don't you worry, I'm going to cook for you.
sentences.zh: 或者我的小儿子总是说，你别担心，我要给你做饭。

sentences.en: I'm like, lovely, that'd be nice.
sentences.zh: 我说，太好了，那挺好的。

sentences.en: But we need to, in order to have that happen, we have to give our kids permission to individuate from us, and to not still be under our constant control.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要，为了让这一切发生，我们必须允许孩子们与我们分化，而不是一直处于我们的持续控制之下。

sentences.en: And even the idea of, you know, once we go into our parental homes, I think sometimes, as soon as I put my keys in the dish
sentences.zh: 甚至这种想法，你知道的，一旦我们回到父母的家里，我想有时候，只要我把钥匙放进那个

sentences.en: where we keep our keys, it's that like ching that suddenly gets you back into being a child.
sentences.zh: 我们放钥匙的盘子里，那种“叮”的一声就突然把你拉回了童年状态。

sentences.en: And you need to grow up as a parent, in order to let your children develop into young adults and beyond.
sentences.zh: 而作为一个父母，你需要成熟起来，以便让你的孩子成长为年轻人及至更远。

sentences.en: And you can't still expect to control all of their behaviours.
sentences.zh: 你不能依然期望控制他们所有的行为。

sentences.en: It's like, I can allow you to make an unwise decision that I don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，我可以允许你做出我不赞同的并不明智的决定。

sentences.en: I can't necessarily allow you to make an unsafe decision as a child.
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我不一定能允许你做出不安全的决定。

sentences.en: But even those small amounts of autonomy are so important, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但即使是那些微量的自主权也是如此重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the thing is, I mean, nothing is more threatening to somebody who is high in psychopathic
sentences.zh: 问题是，我的意思是，没有什么比那些精神病态特质

sentences.en: traits than individuation, as having not just a child, you know, a child is kind of the purest example of this.
sentences.zh: 很高的人更害怕分化了，不仅仅是面对一个孩子，你知道，孩子可以说是这方面最纯粹的例子。

sentences.en: But, you know, for anybody who finds themselves within the orbit of a psychopath,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，对于任何发现自己处在精神病态者磁场范围之内的人来说，

sentences.en: any sense of individuation, any sense of not entirely agreeing, not entirely buying into their world view, is immensely threatening.
sentences.zh: 任何分化的意识，任何不完全赞同、不完全买账他们的世界观的意识，都是极其具有威胁性的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you see the wealth of research in psychopathy has been done in organisational psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会发现大量关于精神病态的研究都是在组织心理学中进行的。

sentences.en: So, you know, within workplace environments.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在职场环境中。

sentences.en: And, you know, you see it there that anybody who finds themselves with a psychopathic boss, that's a classic example, that the level of control exerted will be staggering.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在那里面能看到，任何发现自己有个精神病态老板的人，这就是一个经典的例子，其施加的控制程度会是惊人的。

sentences.en: You know, I gave an example in the book of staff being unable to decide what colour to paint a toilet in case they got into trouble, you know, and it's that level of control.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在书中举过一个例子，员工甚至无法决定把洗手间粉刷成什么颜色，生怕惹上麻烦，你知道，就是那种程度的控制。

sentences.en: And I think we see that throughout the psychopaths' behavioural repertoire, it is very much about, I will enter a social situation
sentences.zh: 我想我们在精神病态者的行为组合中随处都能看到这一点，这很大程度上在于：我会进入一个社交场合，

sentences.en: and I will take charge of it and I will control not just how that social situation goes, but how you think about it, which is what is so damaging to everybody around them.
sentences.zh: 然后我会接管它，我不仅要控制这个社交场合的走向，还要控制你对它的看法，而这正是对他们身边所有人最具破坏性的地方。

sentences.en: So interesting.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: So interesting.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: So you kind of teased us at the beginning that you can tell a psychopath straight away.
sentences.zh: 所以你一开始吊了我们的胃口，说你一眼就能看出谁是精神病态者。

sentences.en: So I'm going to keep my hands out of the way when I ask you, when I ask you that question, Emma.
sentences.zh: 所以当我问你问题时，艾玛，我要把手放好别乱动。

sentences.en: Tell us about some of the things that people might be able to look out for.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲人们可以留意的一些迹象吧。

sentences.en: Well, so what's really interesting in terms of psychopathy is you can, evidence suggests,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以关于精神病态，非常有趣的是，你可以，有证据表明，

sentences.en: research has shown that we can detect psychopathy from what's called thin slice behavioural examples.
sentences.zh: 研究已经表明我们可以从所谓的微观行为样本中检测出精神病态。

sentences.en: So if you see somebody from across a room, we do have the capacity to pick up psychopathic traits.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你从房间的另一端看到某个人，我们确实有能力察觉到精神病态的特质。

sentences.en: However, the problem comes when we start to communicate with that person.
sentences.zh: 然而，问题出在我们开始与那个人交流的时候。

sentences.en: What we know is that when that thin slice becomes a bit thicker, critically, once they start talking to us, we lose the capacity to assess psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，当那个微观样本变得稍微厚重一点时，至关重要的是，一旦他们开始和我们说话，我们就失去了评估精神病态的能力。

sentences.en: And I think one of the reasons that that happens is the killer blow of psychopathic charm.
sentences.zh: 我想之所以会这样，其中一个原因就是精神病态魅力的致命一击。

sentences.en: Nothing fascinates me quite as much as psychopathic charm, because in terms of, you know, about their need to control an environment, this is how we do it.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比精神病态的魅力更让我着迷的了，因为就，你知道的，关于他们控制环境的需求而言，这就是我们如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: Because they are, they have the ability
sentences.zh: 因为他们是，他们有能力

sentences.en: to lock you in, to talk to you in a way that you, you stop questioning.
sentences.zh: 把你锁住，以一种让你停止质疑的方式跟你说话。

sentences.en: There's some, there's some fantastic research in the book.
sentences.zh: 书中提到了一些非常棒的研究。

sentences.en: Not my research, that's not me blowing my own trumpet.
sentences.zh: 不是我的研究，我可不是在自吹自擂。

sentences.en: There is just some really interesting research about what happens when we find ourselves face to face with somebody who's very high in charisma.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常有趣的研究，关于当我们发现自己面对一个极具个人魅力的人时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And research has shown that if we are in communication with somebody who's very charismatic, we see a reduced blood flow in the prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果我们与一个极具魅力的人进行交流，我们会发现前额叶皮层的血流量减少了。

sentences.en: The prefrontal cortex is critical for all our smart stuff, you know, all our logical thinking, rational thinking,
sentences.zh: 前额叶皮层对于我们所有的聪明才智至关重要，你知道，所有逻辑思维、理性思维，

sentences.en: our ability to tell if somebody is lying to us.
sentences.zh: 以及我们辨别某人是否在对我们说谎的能力。

sentences.en: What they termed it the guru effect.
sentences.zh: 他们把这称之为“古鲁效应”（guru effect）。

sentences.en: This is so cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: This is this is why I love psychology.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我热爱心理学。

sentences.en: Because they called it the guru effect.
sentences.zh: 因为他们把它叫做“古鲁效应”。

sentences.en: Because when you are face to face with somebody like a guru, who's highly charismatic, you actually become a bit stupider.
sentences.zh: 因为当你面对像古鲁这样极具魅力的人时，你实际上会变得有点变笨了。

sentences.en: Um, and there is, there is an evolutionary, um, logic to it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且这里面，嗯，有一种演化上的逻辑。

sentences.en: In evolutionary terms, we read charisma or charm as being a social signal.
sentences.zh: 在演化层面上，我们将个人魅力或迷人之处解读为一个社会信号。

sentences.en: This tells us somebody knows what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我们，这个人知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: This person is capable, you know, if this person is, is capable, um, high in social status, I don't need to reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 这个人是有能力的，你知道，如果这个人是，是有能力的，嗯，社会地位很高，我不需要重新发明轮子。

sentences.en: I can just assume they know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我可以直接假设他们知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Ergo, I can stop thinking so hard and let them take control.
sentences.zh: 因此，我可以不用思考得那么累，让他们来掌控一切。

sentences.en: You know, as a psychopath, you don't want anything more than that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为一个精神病态者，你再渴望不过了。

sentences.en: You know, that is a phenomenal tool to have in your arsenal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是你武器库里一个非凡的工具。

sentences.en: But the problem comes, of course, when you walk away and you go, wait, what did I just agree to?
sentences.zh: 但问题当然在于，当你走开时，你会想：等等，我刚才都答应了些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that is so funny.
sentences.zh: 是的，太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Um, and there's something around the smile and the hand gestures and the fact that if, if you don't let the psychopath get to you, you can observe their psychopathy in 33
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有关于微笑、手势以及这样一个事实：如果，如果你不让精神病态者影响到你，你可以在33

sentences.en: milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 毫秒内观察出他们的精神病态。

sentences.en: I think once you give them a chance to start working on you, they get your defenses down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我想一旦你给他们机会开始对你施加影响，他们就会让你的防线稍稍卸下。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: You know, and, and this is exactly what's happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这正是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, as, as humans, part of what we do is read the environment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，作为人类，我们所做的事情之一就是解读周围环境。

sentences.en: Um, you know, we, we, we, we bad mouth hypervigilance, but it's very useful in terms of keeping us alive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我们，我们，我们总贬低过度警惕，但它在让我们保持生存方面非常有用。

sentences.en: Um, and one of the threats in the environment is potentially other people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，环境中的威胁之一可能就是其他人。

sentences.en: So psychopathy does come with signals, uh, you know, so one of the classic ones, um, that always gets my spidey senses tingling is somebody who stands that little bit too close to
sentences.zh: 所以精神病态确实伴随着信号，呃，你知道的，所以其中一个经典的信号，呃，总是让我感到警觉的是，有人站得离我

sentences.en: me.
sentences.zh: 太近了。

sentences.en: Um, you know, somebody who doesn't respect, uh, interpersonal space.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，一个不尊重，呃，人际空间的人。

sentences.en: There are, there are standards for interpersonal space who we will allow into what radius, you know, the closer we are to somebody, the closer we allow them to stand.
sentences.zh: 人际空间是有标准的，我们允许谁进入什么半径，你知道，我们离某人越近，我们允许他们站得越近。

sentences.en: Um, but psychopaths just go, yeah, I'm just going to stand where I want to stand.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是精神病态者只会觉得，好吧，我想站在哪儿就站在哪儿。

sentences.en: Um, uh, and, and that is a really powerful evolutionary signal because that tells us this person isn't playing by our social rules.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，而且，这是一个非常强有力的演化信号，因为这告诉我们这个人不按我们的社会规则行事。

sentences.en: Um, and what that should do is signal a threat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而这本该发出威胁的信号。

sentences.en: But of course, once they start talking, the bit of the brain that's like, hi, hi, this isn't okay.
sentences.zh: 但当然，一旦他们开始说话，大脑里那个在喊着“嘿，嘿，这不对劲”的部分，

sentences.en: Um, tends to clock off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，往往就下线了。

sentences.en: So it becomes a lot harder.
sentences.zh: 所以这就变得困难得多了。

sentences.en: So it's all about people say, how do you detect psychopathy?

sentences.en: Talk to us briefly about trauma bonding, Emma.

sentences.en: Trauma bonding is critical when you're looking at psychopathy and long-term relationships, not just romantic, but parental.

sentences.en: Any long-lasting relationship with a psychopath will have an element of trauma bonding.
sentences.zh: 与精神病态者的任何持久关系中都会包含创伤纽带的成分。

sentences.en: Remember, this person has told you you're useless.
sentences.zh: 记住，这个人已经对你说过你很没用。

sentences.en: This person has not only told you, they've convinced you that you are incapable, that you are worthless, that nobody else will want you.
sentences.zh: 这个人不仅对你说过，他们还让你深信自己无能，一无是处，不会再有人想要你。

sentences.en: And so the logical thing to do is to cling on to whoever is willing to have you because you have lost any confidence that you can start again and let alone start again alone.
sentences.zh: 所以合乎逻辑的做法是死死抓住任何愿意要你的人，因为你已经失去了从头开始的任何信心，更不用说独自重新开始了。

sentences.en: So trauma bond, that creation of a trauma bond, I would say is almost the end goal.
sentences.zh: 因此，创伤纽带，这种创伤纽带的建立，可以说是最终的目标。

sentences.en: After the love bombing comes the gaslighting, the emotional manipulation, the lies, and that destruction of your sense of self.
sentences.zh: 在爱情轰炸之后，便是煤气灯操纵、情感操控、谎言，以及对你自我认知的摧毁。

sentences.en: Once that has happened, you are locked in because you no longer feel capable of escaping.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些发生了，你就被彻底锁死了，因为你不再觉得自己有能力逃脱。

sentences.en: Gosh, if someone is watching or listening to this as a single person,

sentences.en: They're not all like that.

sentences.en: If they can be loving at the beginning of a relationship, why can't they sustain that all the time?
sentences.zh: 如果他们在恋爱初期可以表现得很慈爱，为什么他们不能一直保持那样呢？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: So I think what we have to recognise in psychopathy is that just like empathy,
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们必须认识到，在精神病态中，就像同理心一样，

sentences.en: lovingness, kindness, generosity are all motivated behaviours.
sentences.zh: 充满爱意、善良、慷慨全都是有动机的行为。

sentences.en: Now, I mean, that's true for all of us.
sentences.zh: 现在我的意思是，这对我们所有人来说都是如此。

sentences.en: In a heatwave, few of us are loving, generous and nice.
sentences.zh: 在热浪中，我们很少有人能做到充满爱意、慷慨大方和友善。

sentences.en: So we all have that element of motivation when we behave well towards others.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们对他人表现好时，我们都有那种动机的成分。

sentences.en: However, when we are talking about our closest social circle, that for most of us, that tends to be removed.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们谈论我们最亲密的社交圈时，对大多数人来说，那种动机往往就不存在了。

sentences.en: We treat them well because we treat them well, because they're our children.
sentences.zh: 我们对他们好，纯粹是因为我们对他们好，因为他们是我们的孩子。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会这样做。

sentences.en: For a psychopath, that is different.
sentences.zh: 但对于精神病态者来说，情况则不同。

sentences.en: One of the fascinating things I came across when writing the book is inverted social reward.
sentences.zh: 我在写书时遇到的最吸引人的事情之一就是倒置的社交奖赏。

sentences.en: Most of us get a dopamine rush from interacting well with others, from having a nice conversation, you know, from getting on well and having a good laugh.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人从与他人的良好互动中、从愉快的对话中、你知道的，从相处融洽和开怀大笑中，都能获得多巴胺的飙升。

sentences.en: Most of us get a sense of reward from that, a dopamine rush.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人从中获得一种奖赏感，一种多巴胺的冲击。

sentences.en: Psychopaths do not.
sentences.zh: 精神病态者则不然。

sentences.en: What has been, what research has shown is that they instead experience an inverted sense of social reward.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，他们经历的其实是一种倒置的社交奖赏感。

sentences.en: So they will get their dopamine rush from creating carnage.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会从制造混乱中获得多巴胺的飙升。

sentences.en: They will get a sense of reward from causing trouble, starting arguments.
sentences.zh: 他们会从惹事生非、挑起争端中获得奖赏感。

sentences.en: If you ever heard that person's always spoiling for a fight, that's why, because they genuinely will feel a rush of reward from that negative social interaction.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过某人总是唯恐天下不乱，那就是原因所在，因为他们确实会从那种消极的社交互动中感受到奖赏的冲击。

sentences.en: The other thing that's related to psychopathy is negative social potency.
sentences.zh: 与精神病态相关的另一件事是消极社交效能。

sentences.en: You know, that having the power to cause trouble in a relationship is really appealing to psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在一段关系中拥有挑起事端的力量，对精神病态者来说极具吸引力。

sentences.en: So you will never get them maintaining the niceness because it's just not rewarding.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远不会让他们保持友善，因为那根本无法带给他们奖赏感。

sentences.en: Gosh, wow, that really is food for thought, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 天哪，哇，这真令人深思，不是吗？

sentences.en: Like, watch out.

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
